items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: Implements exactly the reported fix: isCodexCliAvailable() and probeReadiness()'s codex arm now resolve via win32-spawn's resolveSpawn (ADR-044) instead of defaultRun on Windows; verified both call sites (the only two `defaultRun("codex", ...)` uses in server/src), no extra features added.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: resolveSpawn's null return (unresolvable bare name) is mapped to a RunResult {ok:false, code:null}, matching the pre-existing ENOENT contract; execFile errors flow through the same parseExecResult helper as defaultRun so the ok/code semantics stay identical.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input reaches the spawned command or args (both are hardcoded literals: "codex"/"--version"); resolveSpawn/win32CmdWrap are the existing, already-reviewed ADR-044 module, unmodified; no secrets touched.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: New tests assert on outcomes (ok/stdout/code), including a real regression-reproduction test (a genuine .cmd shim on PATH) that proves defaultRun fails on it and defaultRunShim succeeds — run and passing on an actual Windows host, not mocked.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: Single subprocess spawn per probe, same as before; no loops, no DB, no change to the existing parallel Promise.all readiness-arm structure.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: All touched files stay well under the 300-LOC guideline (largest is readiness-probe.ts at 285, pre-existing); defaultRunShim lives beside defaultRun in readiness-probe-run.ts, the same module that already owns the probe-runner primitives; parseExecResult factored out to avoid duplicating the ok/code parsing between the two.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: No serialized format (JSON/YAML/config file) is produced or consumed by this change — it changes how a subprocess is spawned/resolved, not a producer/consumer file boundary. classify_complexity.py returned no risk_flags (touches_io_boundary did not fire).

items.name: Test Hygiene Probe
items.note: uv run scan_test_hygiene.py --diff reported "no findings" against the working-tree diff.
